title: PRP in ACLR to Prevent PTOA
official: Platelet Rich Plasma (PRP) Treatment of the Anterior Cruciate Ligament Injured Knee to Decrease the Risk of Post-traumatic Osteoarthritis (PTOA): a Randomized Double-blind Controlled Trial
summary: The purpose of our study is to examine the effect of platelet-rich-plasma (PRP) injection on the short-term resolution of post-injury inflammation (biomarkers) and improvement in joint function in patients with acute ACL injury. This RCT has been powered based on the questionnaire KOOS Jr. but it is considered a 'pilot study' in terms of the lab analysis proposed.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Acute ACL injury within 6 weeks of presentation
* Age 14-50
* Male or female
* Meniscus injury that can be treated with meniscectomy or repair (the lack of meniscus injury will not exclude patients)

Exclusion Criteria:

* Prior ACL reconstruction
* Prior cartilage repair procedure
* Prior meniscus surgery within 12 months
* Prior steroid, hyaluronic acid, or PRP injection within 6 months
* Other ligament injury requiring repair
* Any cartilage lesion requiring repair
* Any cartilage lesion greater than grade 2 (partial thickness injury)
* History of inflammatory arthritis or joint sepsis
* Non English speakers
sponsor: Hospital for Special Surgery, New York
